title: Make room after the goalie whistle
objective: Recognize possession and space after a scoped goalie-freeze restart.
briefing: In the named Hockey Canada U9 half-ice model, a goalie-freeze whistle gives the defending team possession and asks attackers to retreat. The gold goalie already held the puck and the whistle happened. Gold1 now controls the restart puck near the crease; YOU are a navy attacker asked to back away. Earlier events are stated, not animated. Navy attacks the +x end; gold attacks the -x end. The full rink is an orientation map for this small activity.
cues: The goalie freeze and whistle already happened.
Gold1 now has restart possession.
The crease is near the gold goal.

questions.prompt: Why do you need to give Gold1 room before play continues?
questions.explanation: In this named Hockey Canada U9 half-ice model, attackers back off three metres after the goalie freezes the puck. That gives the defending team room to restart with possession. Follow the instructions for your local game format; do not assume every North American U9 program uses this restart.

title: A return option around the circle
objective: Find a new return angle after a completed pass near a faceoff circle.
briefing: YOU just passed to Navy2 near the faceoff circle in the attacking end. Navy2 controls the puck now. Gold1 has moved onto the old straight return line; that movement is stated, not animated. Navy3 waits closer to the boards. Find a new place to support Navy2 rather than demanding the same return. Navy attacks the +x end; gold attacks the -x end. The full rink is an orientation map for this small activity.
cues: Navy2 has the puck near the circle centre.
Gold1 occupies the old return line.
Navy3 is closer to the boards.
